A1.justification: Both PDFs describe RePo and contain readable text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–D. Matching retained content across renumbering and relocation supports a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original OLMo-2 1B evaluations, attention and position analyses, and GPT-2 text-reversal experiments in Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds OLMo-2 7B evaluations in Tables 1–3 and 5 and Appendix B.4.

M1.justification: The SwiGLU position representation, per-head scalar position assignment, attention equations, and autoregressive procedure remain unchanged. The one-third-depth rule selects the existing starting-layer hyperparameter for different model sizes; the 1B configuration still starts at layer 5.

E1.justification: v2 removes NLGraph graph reasoning, RULER aggregation and variable tracking, and LongBench TREC classification, substantially narrowing task coverage. RULER QA remains in the long-context plots. The four-variant NIAH breakdown does not establish that these variants were absent from v1's aggregate evaluation.

E2.justification: RoPE, NoPE, R2N1, and N2R1 remain the baselines in matched 1B comparisons, and the reversal experiment retains RoPE and NoPE. The new 7B experiments reuse RoPE; no new comparison method is introduced or removed from retained comparisons.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 adds a substantial 7B experimental configuration, comparing RePo with RoPE and starting RePo at layer 10. The 50B-token continual-training budget, 4096-token training context, existing 1B configuration, and YaRN extrapolation settings are retained.

E4.justification: Appendix B.4 and Figure 5 extend the length-extrapolation robustness test to 7B models at 4K, 8K, and 16K tokens. The starting-layer ablation, attention-mass and position-pattern analyses, reversal study, and case study remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The additional results retain the same point-estimate reporting practice; descriptive position statistics are also unchanged.

E6.justification: Table 1 replaces mixed-task RULER averages of 44.64/55.68 for RoPE/RePo with four-variant NIAH averages of 85.9/91.3; these are different task sets. Removing TREC changes the 1B RePo LongBench average from 28.31 to 27.86 while retained task scores remain unchanged. New 7B RePo/RoPE results include 37.61/33.52 on HybridQA, 32.03/25.65 on LongBench, and 70.30/70.92 on general tasks. Figure 5 adds 7B extrapolation results.

T1.justification: Equations 1–8, the NoPE constant-position equivalence in Appendix A, and the position-pattern definitions are retained. A position-index notation correction does not alter the mathematics.

C1.justification: The central benefits claimed for context re-positioning remain. The abstract and introduction extend their empirical scope to 7B and explicitly claim effective scaling with model capacity. The introduction also replaces minimum gains over competing baselines with gains against RoPE on the revised evaluations.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations about scaling and preserving latent structural cues in tables. It removes the interpretation that NoPE's graph advantage challenges locality assumptions, alongside the introduction's probabilistic argument about fixed positions being least informative. The main CLT and attention explanations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix B.1 adds exact OLMES identifiers for four NIAH tasks, and Section 4.1 discloses the stage-1 token count and 7B layer configuration. The abstract adds prospective code-and-model-weight release language while retaining the repository link; it does not establish newly available resources.

R1.justification: Related work gains brief discussions of Forgetting Transformer, Path Attention, Selective RoPE, attention sorting, and newer RoPE studies, plus contamination references supporting model selection. The NLGraph citation is removed. The central comparison with CoPE and orthogonality framing remain.

P1.justification: v2 revises portions of the abstract, introduction, experimental setup, results, and related work; reorders the structured-data discussion; expands Appendix B; and adds Deng Cai to the author list. The overall narrative structure and most method and analysis prose remain intact.

P2.justification: Tables 1–3 and 5 gain model-size groupings and differences from RoPE, with task-column changes where coverage narrows. The opening radar chart is removed, a 7B extrapolation plot is added, and appendix figures move. Retained plots themselves are unchanged.

improvement.justification: The controlled 7B evaluations reduce the main claims' dependence on a single small backbone, while explicit NIAH task identifiers and expanded related work improve reproducibility and positioning. These provide a modest net gain. The benefit is limited by removing graph, aggregation, variable-tracking, and TREC evidence and by comparing only against RoPE at 7B; the core method and diagnostic analyses remain unchanged.
